title: Exotic legal/economic structures belong in evidence and policy, not the double-entry engine
summary: Trusts, SPVs, legal-versus-beneficial ownership, collateral, hypothecation/rehypothecation, reinsurance, derivatives, consolidation and future reporting bases can all affect accounting treatment. Accounting Core carries open evidence-bearing dimensions and exact policy identity so these structures can evolve without modifying the core posting mechanics.
invariants: Accounting Core does not infer ownership, control, economic risk, derecognition or consolidation conclusions from a transaction name.
Company policy may inspect authoritative legal/economic evidence and emit the appropriate journal draft.
Open dimensions can preserve legal owner, beneficial owner, risk bearer, encumbrance, trust/vehicle, counterparty, valuation basis and other future evidence.
A new exotic structure should normally require a new/versioned policy or evidence schema, not a fork of AccountingBook.
The core remains responsible for mechanics: account/period checks, exact currency balancing, evidence binding, immutability and reversal rather than mutation.

provenance.claim: Trusts, ownership, collateral, rehypothecation, reinsurance, derivatives and consolidation semantics belong to entity policy/evidence, not core mechanics.
